newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani stocks end up, seen range-bounded.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani stocks end up, seen range-bounded.

text.p: Pakistani stocks finished higher on Tuesday amid a rally prompted by a government relief package for the stock market, but dealers said the index was likely to remain range-bounded on Wednesday.
"The sentiment is positive but there is still a lot of selling by small players," ING Baring Securities sales chief Samir Ahmad said. The selling might keep the rise restricted.

The Karachi Stock Exchange (KSE) 100-share index rose 21.64 points, or 1.48 percent, to end at 1,484.18. Gainers led losers 181 to 99. Turnover fell to 40.50 million shares from 42.40 million on Monday.

Bank of Punjab rose 0.20 to 18.80 rupees, Adamjee Insurance 10.25 to 105, Askari General Insurance 2.0 to 22, EFU Life Assurance 1.50 to 13 and Commercial Union Assurance 1.35 to 15.60. Dewan Salman Fibre rose 1.25 to 35.75, Hub Power Co 1.0 to 35.20. PTCL rose 0.45 to 27.80 and ICI Pakistan rose 2.10 to 22.60.
